title: What should the Celix SBOM describe?
subtitle: Specimen 001 · Apache Celix PR #845
issueQuestion: What exactly should an Apache Celix SBOM describe, and what does that evidence warrant?

nodes.label: Generate a CycloneDX SBOM in Conan CI
nodes.text: The initial proposal adds CycloneDX generation to the existing Conan CI and publishes the result as build evidence.
nodes.author: Robert McConnell

nodes.label: An SBOM needs a concrete artifact boundary
nodes.text: A recipe or test workflow is not the final binary. Dependency overrides can change the resolved binary graph and therefore change the corresponding SBOM without changing Celix source.
nodes.author: PengZheng

nodes.label: Bind the SBOM to the deployed Conan graph
nodes.text: The revised workflow consumes the created Celix Conan package, deploys the resolved binary packages, and generates the CycloneDX SBOM from that same dependency-graph resolution. The publication step uses -b never so it cannot silently rebuild another configuration.
nodes.author: Robert McConnell

nodes.label: But Celix does not make a binary release
nodes.text: The revised workflow is still testing infrastructure, not a release process. Celix primarily releases source and does not currently maintain a canonical binary distribution.
nodes.author: PengZheng / pnoltes

nodes.label: Use a reproducible reference dependency state
nodes.text: A representative Conan lockfile can preserve a resolved dependency list for a documented Celix configuration and provide the reference state for an SBOM, reproducible development builds, and vulnerability scanning.
nodes.author: pnoltes

nodes.label: The reference state is a safe default, not a universal Celix graph
nodes.text: The lockfile and SBOM should describe a documented safe-default dependency state while users remain free to change dependency versions and options for their own builds.
nodes.author: PengZheng / pnoltes

nodes.label: The reference graph can be audited
nodes.text: Conan Audit can assess vulnerabilities in the dependency state selected by the documented default resolution, giving the project a concrete security-maintenance target without claiming to describe every downstream build.
nodes.author: PengZheng

nodes.label: A development container may be a concrete maintained artifact
nodes.text: Instead of inventing an official Celix binary distribution, the project may provide and maintain a development container as a concrete artifact that helps users build applications with Celix.
nodes.author: pnoltes

nodes.label: Open: what does Celix ultimately warrant?
nodes.text: The discussion has converged on a safe-default lockfile plus SBOM, but the precise relationship among the source release, reference dependency state, vulnerability reports, and any maintained development-container artifact remains to be implemented and made authoritative upstream.
nodes.author: Horn reconstruction
